eval-8 (bulk-mixed) without_skill hit a soft failure not caught by assertions: it filtered on a guessed 'name' field, got a 400 BAD_REQUEST, then recovered with 'title'. The skill's 'inspect, then act - use only those field names' rule prevents this class of wasted round trip.
Skill cost: +43% tokens (42.3k vs 29.6k mean... see per-run) and ~+13s mean time, spent almost entirely on the mandated describe_schema/describe_collection step before acting.

Read-only and single-write evals (2,3,4,5) are handled equally well by both configs - Claude's default MCP handling is already strong there. The skill's marginal value concentrates in (a) forcing schema inspection so field-name guesses can't slip through, and (b) the destructive-op confirmation discipline in eval-6.

Assertions that never discriminate in this run: 'uses filter_template with placeholder', 'single bulk_write for batch', 'confirm_count matches real count', 'no writes on read tasks' - both configs already satisfy these. They still guard against regressions but don't show skill lift here.
Single run per cell - no variance data. A rerun with 3x per cell would show whether the eval-1 baseline miss is consistent or a coin flip.
